summary: Find the arithmetic mean of a numeric field.
syntax: SELECT AVG(amount) AS average_name FROM table_name;
documentation: AVG computes the average of non-NULL values and returns a floating-point result when inputs exist. It returns NULL for an empty non-NULL input set.
caution: NULL values are excluded from both the total and the count. SQLite may coerce nonnumeric text, so validate imported data.
title: Average the order amounts
problem: Return one column called average_cents with the average amount_cents from orders. Return SQL NULL when there are no non-NULL amounts.
goal: Use AVG() or an equivalent approach that demonstrates the same concept.
hint: Use AVG(amount_cents) with the expected alias.
starter:
-- Write one SELECT query against the example tables.
SELECT 1;

tests.name: Two orders
tests.setup:
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER, customer TEXT, amount_cents INTEGER, status TEXT);
INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1, 'Ava', 100, 'paid'), (2, 'Micki', 300, 'paid');

tests.name: NULL amount excluded
tests.setup:
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER, customer TEXT, amount_cents INTEGER, status TEXT);
INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1, 'Ava', 100, 'paid'), (2, 'Micki', NULL, 'paid');
